ety.text: Ancient Greek ἄσυλον (ásulon)bor. Latin asȳlumlbor. English asylum Learned borrowing from Latin asȳlum, borrowed from Ancient Greek ἄσυλον (ásulon).

senses.d: A place of safety or refuge.
The protection, physical and legal, afforded by such a place (as, for example, for political refugees).
A place of protection or restraint for one or more classes of the disadvantaged, especially the mentally ill.

ex: It was she who in the last few years had spread abroad the notion that Charles Nagle, in the public interest, should be asylumed.
We have..sheltered its paupers, asylumed its orphans, clothed its nakedness.
